extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians (especially early-career) who want to perform peer review for medical journals, particularly case reports
extracted.subtask_short: peer review of medical case reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for clinicians and researchers on how to perform high-quality peer reviews of case reports for medical journals, including whether to accept invitations, how to read and evaluate manuscript sections, writing comments, and ethical/confidentiality considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a high-quality peer review, you must dedicate the appropriate amount of time to the task since the peer review process is a responsibility that has a significant impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must complete their peer review on time as delayed submission can negatively affect the journal's publication time; editors face dilemmas when reviews are late. For a first peer review of a case report, spend at least a few hours: get familiar with the topic area, review the manuscript, then review again. Time required decreases with experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate expertise before accepting
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are often seeking an expert opinion regarding the manuscript. Therefore, you must know the topic well before you accept to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not an expert on rare conditions, perform an appropriate literature review (including the reference list) to learn enough to provide an expert opinion. Example: a condition may appear rare at one center but common at a tertiary center—be mindful of context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is critical to maintain confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscript content or use privileged information outside the review process; treat manuscripts as confidential documents throughout the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline when conflicts or insufficient knowledge exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowing when to decline a peer review invitation is critical, even if you are an expert in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples meriting decline: conflict of interest, collaborator of the study, personal knowledge of the study, same institution, or lack of knowledge about the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial evaluation: overall flow, linguistics, and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial evaluation should focus on the overall flow, linguistics, and quality assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take notes externally; screen for overall readability, organization, and obvious methodological or reporting problems before diving into details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title reflects content and central message
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should reflect the content and central message of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many readers screen by title; assess appropriateness and accuracy. Ensure consistency between title and abstract/content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract contains current knowledge, unknowns, and learning point
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should contain the current knowledge related to the case and unknown content related to the topic. It would be helpful to see the manuscript's learning point or core message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that abstract summarizes the clinical significance, learning points, and is consistent with manuscript findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction provides pertinent, accurate background and states contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction should not be a list of literature reviews. This section should reflect pertinent and accurate background information related to the topic and how this manuscript will add new knowledge to the current literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to perform a literature search and provide related essential studies in their comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case description: conciseness, diagnostic accuracy, and treatment appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The case should be concise and appropriate for the scope of the journal. Reviewers should ensure the accuracy of the diagnosis with pertinent positives and negatives and the appropriateness of the treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors used a novel method, request a comparison to the standard of care. Ensure inclusion of appropriate, high-quality images (radiographic, endoscopic, pathology) when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion should support the learning point and acknowledge limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion should lead to the main learning point of the manuscript. The authors' arguments should support the conclusion by providing an appropriate literature review of the content and highlighting its uniqueness. Appropriate disclosure of the manuscript's limitations and the topic's future direction should be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that conclusions are supported by evidence and that limitations and future directions are explicitly discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: References must be accurate and relevant; self-citation appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check each reference closely to ensure the authors cited important and relevant studies. When authors cite their previous studies in the current manuscript, it is considered self-citation. Reviewers should ensure that self-citations are appropriately employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing key citations, irrelevant or inaccurate references, and inappropriate self-promotion via excessive self-citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments: comprehensive, succinct, accurate, respectful
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should be comprehensive, succinct, and accurate, and comment on the importance, novelty, and impact of the study. It is helpful to give constructive feedback to their colleagues since respectful comments are the key to a good peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid degrading comments. Treat reviewers as consultants whose recommendations should be taken seriously; provide constructive, actionable feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of reviewer comments: summary then main points and improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sentences of the review should summarize the manuscript and show the clinical significance. The subsequent sentences should point out the main learning points of the manuscript and explain how this manuscript can be improved. Lastly, the suitability and relevance of the manuscript should be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a concise summary and significance, then list strengths and areas for improvement with clear suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not state publication decision in comments to authors; use confidential editor comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer should avoid including the comments regarding the decision for publication. You should include your recommendation in the confidential comments to the editors and provide rationale for the recommended decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors make the final decision; give a recommendation and rationale privately to editors and keep author-facing comments focused on improvement. Attempt to minimize bias in recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish major vs minor points
rubrics_metrics.description: Major points describe suggested changes that require considerable effort for revision. Minor points should address nonfatal errors such as grammatical or linguistic errors or ambiguous statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State strengths and weaknesses in bullet points with supporting statements and relevant literature for major issues; ensure data accuracy. For minor points, list grammatical fixes, clarifications, figure/table queries, and suggest helpful references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to editors for ethical/quality concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reviewer has a concern about the quality of the manuscript or ethical concerns, reviewers can address their concerns here. This section is usually confidential and will not be shared with the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a summary of the manuscript with suggested revisions for editors, flag ethical issues, and remember reviewers can only recommend a decision; the final decision rests with editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take notes externally to avoid losing work
rubrics_metrics.description: While reading a manuscript, we suggest taking notes in a separate document. We recommend not using the journal's reviewer page for the comments, as websites can timeout and you risk losing your content before submission of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose and save comments offline, then paste into the submission system when ready to avoid data loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registering and seeking mentorship to start reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal websites often have a link to register as a peer reviewer. You can register by creating an account in the journal's submission system. Alternatively, you can contact the editorial office or ask mentors about pairing up on reviews with supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include your expertise on submission sites to be invited; pairing with mentors is a recommended pathway for early-career reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize bias while reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should attempt to minimize bias while reviewing the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of personal, institutional, or topical biases that may affect judgment; focus on evidence and methodological rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review quality affects future invitations and ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals have a rating system to assess peer review quality. If you provide a peer review which is not comprehensive, editors may not invite you to be a peer reviewer again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive, timely, and constructive reviews to maintain standing with journals and receive future invitations.
